content: 1. Clarithromycin and Phenobarbital: Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of clarithromycin by enhancing the metabolism of the drug through the CYP3A4 enzyme. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Clarithromycin and Phenytoin: Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin and omeprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 3. Clarithromycin and Omeprazole: Omeprazole reduces the absorption of phytoestrogens by increasing gastric pH, which applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unclear. 4. Clarithromycin and Pimavanserin: Clarithromycin increases the levels of pimavanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval, so alternative therapies should be considered. 5. Clarithromycin and Pimozide: Clarithromycin raises pimozide levels by reducing its metabolism, and both drugs increase the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 6. Clarithromycin and Pioglitazone: Clarithromycin increases pioglitazone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 7. Clarithromycin and Piperacillin: Clarithromycin may reduce the effects of piperacillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Clarithromycin and Pirtobrutinib: Clarithromycin increases pirtobrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, the pirtobrutinib dose should be reduced. Avoid this combination if possible. 9. Clarithromycin and Pitavastatin: Clarithromycin increases the risk of pitavastatin toxicity, potentially leading to myopathy. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Clarithromycin and Pitolisant: Clarithromycin increases pitolisant levels and prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 11. Clarithromycin and Polatuzumab Vedotin: Clarithromycin increases the levels of polatuzumab vedotin and its toxic metabolites by inhibiting CYP3A4. Close monitoring is required. 12. Clarithromycin and Pomalidomide: Clarithromycin increases pomalidomide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 13. Clarithromycin and Ponatinib: Clarithromycin increases ponatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the ponatinib dose. Avoid this combination if possible. 14. Clarithromycin and Ponesimod: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 15. Clarithromycin and Posaconazole: Clarithromycin increases posaconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein. Omeprazole reduces posaconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Clarithromycin and Pralsetinib: Clarithromycin increases pralsetinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 17. Clarithromycin and Pravastatin: Clarithromycin increases pravastatin levels, raising the risk of myopathy. Do not exceed a pravastatin dose of 40 mg/day when co-administered with clarithromycin. 18. Clarithromycin and Prednisolone/Prednisone: Clarithromycin increases the levels of these corticosteroids by inhibiting CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Clarithromycin and Primaquine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 20. Clarithromycin and Procaineamide: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 21. Clarithromycin and Progesterone (various forms): Clarithromycin increases progesterone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 22. Clarithromycin and Promethazine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 23. Clarithromycin and Propafenone: Clarithromycin increases propafenone levels and prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 24. Clarithromycin and Protamine: Clarithromycin increases protamine levels by reducing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 25. Clarithromycin and Pyridoxine: Clarithromycin reduces pyridoxine levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Clarithromycin and Quazepam: Clarithromycin increases quazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 27. Clarithromycin and Quetiapine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 28. Clarithromycin and Quinidine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 29. Clarithromycin and Quinine: Clarithromycin increases quinine levels and prolongs the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Clarithromycin and Rivaroxaban: Clarithromycin increases rivaroxaban levels, raising the risk of bleeding. Avoid this combination, especially in patients with impaired renal function. 31. Clarithromycin and Roflumilast: Clarithromycin increases roflumilast levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Clarithromycin and Rosiglitazone: Clarithromycin increases rosiglitazone levels, potentially causing hypoglycemia. Monitor glucose levels closely. 33. Clarithromycin and Rosuvastatin: Clarithromycin increases rosuvastatin toxicity, potentially leading to myopathy. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 34. Clarithromycin and Ruxolitinib: Clarithromycin increases ruxolitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the ruxolitinib dose if co-administration is unavoidable. 35. Clarithromycin and Sacubitril/Valsartan: Clarithromycin increases valsartan levels by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Clarithromycin and Salmeterol: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Clarithromycin and Saxagliptin: Clarithromycin increases saxagliptin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust saxagliptin dosage if co-administered. 38. Clarithromycin and Sildenafil: Clarithromycin increases sildenafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 39. Clarithromycin and Simvastatin: Clarithromycin increases simvastatin levels, raising the risk of rhabdomyolysis. This combination is contraindicated. 40. Clarithromycin and Sotalol: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 41. Clarithromycin and Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir: Clarithromycin increases velpatasvir levels, while omeprazole reduces velpatasvir levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 42. Clarithromycin and Sirolimus: Clarithromycin increases sirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 43. Clarithromycin and Sodium Picosulfate: Clarithromycin reduces the efficacy of sodium picosulfate by altering colonic bacterial flora. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Clarithromycin and Selpercatinib: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 45. Clarithromycin and Selumetinib: Clarithromycin increases selumetinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the selumetinib dose if co-administration is unavoidable. 46. Clarithromycin and Sertraline: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 47. Clarithromycin and Sevoflurane: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. This list highlights the importance of monitoring and adjusting therapy when clarithromycin or omeprazole is co-administered with other medications, particularly those metabolized by CYP3A4 or those that prolong the QTc interval.
